hero.desc: What's in the product, how Free and Pro plans work, what AI does, and which social networks we support. If you don't find it — ask via the form.

0.a: Evix is an AI content studio in a single workspace: ToV quiz, client cores library, AI scripts with analysis, avatars and voices, covers, editing (auto and manual), competitor parsing, and publication tracking.

1.a: No. You post the finished video to the social network yourself, then add the publication to the tracker — with a preview, platform, date, and description. Views and likes are filled in manually or pulled in afterward.

2.q: Can scripts be created from scratch or only 'based on a competitor'?
2.a: Both options work. In the 5-step wizard, the first step is choosing the type: 'based on a competitor' (with virality analysis) or your own topic and key points. Then comes the script, avatar, video generation, and editing.

3.a: Five 'cores' are the shared source of truth for AI: client ToV, marketing and product analysis, account core (what worked), and niche core. The competitor core is currently in development.

4.q: Where do view and like metrics come from?
4.a: In the 'Publications' section, metrics update once the post goes live. The 'Statistics' section — aggregated analytics on reach and retention — is currently marked 'Soon'.

0.q: How many plans are there and how do they differ?
0.a: Two plans: Free — all modules and template-based auto-editing. Pro — the same plus manual editing by a live editor and priority on auto-editing.

1.a: Pricing is discussed individually and depends on video volume and team composition. Leave a request — we'll send a quote tailored to your case.

2.q: Is there a separate plan for agencies?
2.a: Corporate terms for network agencies with high client volume are discussed separately. Reach out via the form — we'll put together a plan tailored to your workflow.

0.q: How does Evix analyze a script?
0.a: The script is checked against groups: hook + retention (main weight), mid-tier criteria (visuals, CTA), and minor criteria. It's also cross-referenced with the ToV, marketing, and product cores, and in 'based on a competitor' mode — with the competitor itself. The output: a score, checklists, and recommendations.

1.q: Can I upload my own voice for an avatar?
1.a: You can add an avatar (photo) and a voice (audio sample) to the catalog — with a choice of gender, style, tone, and emotion. If you don't upload anything, the product uses an imitation for the preview.

2.a: You can add competitors manually, in bulk, or run auto-search by niche (platforms, region, ER, audience size). After parsing, a grid of viral videos opens up with breakdowns by hook, retention, and triggers.

0.a: In the publications tracker: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, VKontakte, and others. In competitor parsing and auto-search, additionally: VK Clips, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, Telegram, Dzen.

1.q: Where do I connect social networks?
1.a: In the client profile and in the data library, the 'Connected social networks' section. In the publication form, you can only select connected platforms.

0.q: What roles are available in the product?
0.a: Owner, technical department, script / editing / publication managers, performers (scriptwriter, editor, publisher), and guest client access. Staff have a separate internal login with demo access.

1.q: How do I assign a client to a staff member?
1.a: When creating a client, the owner immediately selects managers (for scripts, editing, and publications). They in turn assign their own performers. A staff member sees their own clients and locked cards of the others — for team transparency.

2.q: Can I reject a script with a comment?
2.a: Yes. Scripts and edits can be returned with a reason for rejection — the author will see the comment. The same works in the editing queue.

hero.desc: We'll train every team member to use Evix successfully — from first login to confidently running a script through the entire pipeline. No fluff, no generic "one-size-fits-all" courses.

benefits.title: What sets it apart from typical courses
benefits.desc: The training is built around roles and real-world workflows, not a checklist of product modules. Every team member sees exactly what they need.

role.title: Tailored to each role
role.desc: A scriptwriter doesn't need to know parsing settings, and an editor doesn't need the ToV quiz. Each person learns only their part of the workspace.

data.title: On your real data
data.desc: We learn on your actual client cores and scripts — not abstract examples — so everything applies directly to real work.

live.title: Live sessions and Q&A
live.desc: Not recorded videos played at 2x — live calls with the team and answers to specific questions about your process.

analysis.title: Script analysis breakdown
analysis.desc: We teach you to read analysis output: what the hook score means, what to look for in the editor brief, and when a script needs a rewrite.

parsing.title: Parsing and competitor research
parsing.desc: We show how to set up filters for your niche and how to adapt viral formats into your own scripts.

support.title: Post-training support
support.desc: We help it stick — answering questions once your team is working in the workspace on its own.

trainers.title: The people who build the product and work with real studios
trainers.desc: No "generalist trainers." Training is led by people from the Evix team who run through the entire pipeline themselves every day.

product.title: Product team
product.desc: They own the scripts, avatars, editing, and thumbnails modules. They know how every step works from the inside.

curators.title: Client curators
curators.desc: They guide teams through onboarding and know which questions come up first — and why.

editors.title: In-house editors
editors.desc: They join for the editing and thumbnails block. They show what a good editor brief actually looks like.

trainers.footnote: Specific people and roles are agreed at kickoff — matched to your team's composition and your priority modules.

stages.title: Training stage by stage
stages.desc: Each stage is a dedicated session or series of sessions. We move at the team's pace — no rushing.

0.title: Workspace overview
0.desc: We walk through the structure: dashboard, clients, library, avatars, scripts, editing, publishing. We show who sees what.

1.title: Cores and the ToV quiz
1.desc: We teach you how to fill in and maintain client cores: ToV, marketing, product. We unpack how they shape the analysis.

2.title: Script wizard
2.desc: We walk through all five steps: type, script, avatar and voiceover, video generation, editing — on a real client topic.

3.title: Team workflow
3.desc: Approvals, send-backs for revision, editing, and publishing. We break down how the process flows between roles.

contact.title: We'll tailor a program to your team
contact.desc: Tell us about your team and priority modules — we'll send back a program tailored to your case.
